en.headline: Card alerts surge as iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders open
en.dek: After Apple opened online pre-orders at 8pm on Saturday, some Hong Kong cardholders said they received charge notices for new iPhones they had not bought.
body: Apple opened online pre-orders for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at 8pm on Saturday. Through the night, some Hong Kong residents posted that they had received credit-card notifications for Apple Store purchases matching new iPhone prices, in some cases after they said they had failed to complete an order.

Local reports said the notices involved cards issued by several banks, including HSBC, Hang Seng and Standard Chartered. Amounts cited included about HK$10,499, HK$11,499 and HK$13,299. One person said several attempted charges added up to more than HK$60,000. Some said bank hotlines were busy for half an hour or longer.

Fong Po-kiu, honorary president of the Hong Kong Information Technology Federation, said congestion at the start of an iPhone sale is familiar. He said that, on past experience, issuers often do not complete a deduction when an order does not go through, but customers who see unfamiliar alerts should still check with their bank.

Separately, he said some unauthorised orders could use card data obtained earlier if a shop briefly relaxes extra verification to keep checkout moving. He advised anyone seeing unusual activity to ask the bank to pause the card. There has been no official police tally of related reports published overnight.

zh.headline: iPhone 18 Pro預購展開 部分市民收到未下單簽賬通知
zh.dek: 蘋果周六晚上8時開放網上預購後，有香港持卡人表示收到與新機售價相符的信用卡通知，部分人稱自己並未成功下單。
body: 蘋果周六晚上8時開放iPhone 18 Pro及iPhone 18 Pro Max網上預購。至深夜及週日凌晨，有市民在社交平台表示收到信用卡交易通知，金額與新機售價相近，部分人稱自己未能完成預訂，卻仍收到扣賬或授權短訊。
本地報道指，涉及通知的信用卡包括匯豐、恒生及渣打等銀行發出的卡，金額有約10,499元、11,499元及13,299元等。有人稱短時間內出現多筆通知，累計逾6萬元。亦有市民表示銀行熱線繁忙，等候超過半小時。
香港資訊科技商會榮譽會長方保僑表示，新iPhone開放預購時網絡及支付系統擠塞並非首次。他指按過往經驗，訂單未完成時發卡銀行很多時不會完成扣款，但若收到不尋常通知，仍應向銀行查詢。
他又說，若網店為疏導人流而放寬部分短訊或應用程式驗證，先前經釣魚網站或黑市流出的卡資料或會被用於嘗試交易。他建議發現異常活動的客戶立即要求暫停該卡。警方尚未公布與此事相關的報案數字。
